title: Centralize CI toolchain config and replace repeated setup steps with composite action
author: Diego Morales
release_notes: Centralizes versions and toolchain setup used by GitHub workflows behind a single composite action; reduces per-workflow duplication and unifies node/python/rust/java versions. No runtime behavior changes expected for production services.
description:
Motivation:
We have a long-running maintenance tax keeping tool versions synchronized across ~10 GitHub Actions workflows. Small version drift and inconsistent setup snippets caused multiple transient CI failures and made dependency updates error-prone. This PR centralizes toolchain configuration and replaces repeated setup logic with a single composite action (.github/actions/toolchain-setup) and a single source-of-truth config file (.github/toolchain.yml).

What this does (high-level):
- Adds .github/actions/toolchain-setup/action.yml: a composite action that installs Node, Python, Rust, and Java according to a common config file. It wraps setup-node/setup-python/actions-rs/setup-java and pins the recommended versions.
- Adds .github/toolchain.yml: canonical versions and OS-specific overrides (linux/macos).
- Updates CI workflows under .github/workflows/* to call the new composite action instead of repeating setup steps.
- Simplifies matrix definitions by referencing the centralized versions rather than hard-coded strings.
- Removes a few legacy one-off setup snippets that are no longer needed.

Checklist (author):
- [x] Add composite action and config file
- [x] Update CI workflows to use composite
- [x] Run full test matrix locally with act/emulation and on CI
- [x] Coordinate with SDK owners (TS/Python/Go) for any version bumps
- [x] Add brief docs in CONTRIBUTING.md pointing at .github/toolchain.yml

Detailed changes / commit summary:
- commit 1: Add toolchain config and composite helper (action.yml + README + tests)
- commit 2: Replace node/python setup in workflows with uses: ./.github/actions/toolchain-setup
- commit 3: Update workflow matrices to reference .github/toolchain.yml via env interpolation
- commit 4: Address reviewer nits, add fallback for runner OS that doesn't support prebuilt tool caches

Files changed (high-level):
- .github/actions/toolchain-setup/action.yml (new)
- .github/actions/toolchain-setup/README.md (new)
- .github/toolchain.yml (new)
- .github/workflows/ci.yaml (modified)
- .github/workflows/lint.yaml (modified)
- .github/workflows/integration-tests.yaml (modified)
- .github/workflows/release.yaml (modified)
commits_summary: Create composite action toolchain-setup to unify setup steps
Switch CI workflows to call composite action and reference centralized versions
Tweak matrix and add OS fallbacks; update CONTRIBUTING.md
review_comments: Riley Chen (review): Nice consolidation. Two asks: 1) add a matrix fallback when a runner doesn't have the cached toolchain; 2) ensure we still surface the individual version in workflow logs.
Author reply: Added an explicit 'TOOLCHAIN_FALLBACK=true' env path and emit versions during setup. See last commit.
Sofia Patel (review): Could we avoid introducing another action if maintainability becomes an issue? Suggest we make the composite intentionally small and well-documented.
Author reply: Agreed — composite wraps existing community actions only and includes a README with upgrade guidance.
Marta Lopez (approve): Tests ran green in staging; approving assuming no runtime changes.
